auto-loan.title: Solve a vehicle price from a $600 loan-payment budget
auto-loan.inputs: $600 monthly financing budget; 60 months; 6% nominal rate; $5,000 down; manual 7% price-based tax and $500 financed fees.
steps: Discount 60 monthly $600 payments at 0.5% per month to find the supported principal.
Solve principal = vehicle price × 1.07 − $5,000 + $500 under the entered manual tax assumptions.
Keep fuel, insurance and maintenance outside this loan-only budget.

personal-loan.title: Read a separately paid personal-loan fee as net initial cash
personal-loan.inputs: $20,000 loan; 36 months; 12% nominal rate; 3% origination fee.
steps: Enter Paid upfront for the $600 fee; the gross disbursement and separate fee payment net to $19,400 at time zero.
Amortize $20,000 over 36 months; no insurance is entered.
Subtract net initial cash from total installments without adding the fee a second time.
personal-loan.answer: Payment: $664.29; total outflow minus net cash: $4,514.30.

personal-loan.title: Separate $20 monthly insurance from loan interest
personal-loan.inputs: $20,000 loan; 36 months; 12% nominal rate; 3% origination fee.
steps: Deduct the 3% fee from $20,000, leaving $19,400 net cash.
Add $20 per month to the principal-and-interest installment; 36 insurance payments total $720.
Use the combined payment for modeled cash-flow APR, without asserting regulatory charge treatment.
personal-loan.answer: Payment including insurance: $684.29; total installment outflow: $24,634.30.

student-loan.title: Add $1,200 annually to a student loan
steps: Keep the original $333.0615 contractual monthly installment.
Add $1,200 at month 12 and each twelfth payment afterward.
Recalculate interest on the reduced balance and cap the final payment at the amount owed.

student-loan.title: Make one $1,200 extra student-loan payment
steps: Keep the original $333.0615 contractual monthly installment.
Add $1,200 at the first scheduled payment only, after that month’s interest.
Recalculate interest on the reduced balance and cap the final payment at the amount owed.
